title: Eight matched TESS pairs retain a CPV spectral line-width excess after speed and temperature control
abstract: We test whether the reported broad spectral lines of complex periodic variable (CPV) hosts remain after matching controls on equatorial speed and temperature. We use eight TESS hosts and 119 controls with public TIC v8.2 and APOGEE DR17 values. Matching without replacement in the same age class gives a geometric mean host-to-control ratio of cross-correlation width divided by equatorial speed of 1.61, with a paired bootstrap 95% interval of 1.21 to 2.13. The exact one-sided sign-randomization probability is 0.0156 under pairwise label exchangeability. Tested matching weights, signal-to-noise and binary cuts retain the positive contrast. The youngest-class subset has six pairs and p = 0.0625. A hidden selection odds ratio of 1.54 can raise the worst-case main probability to 0.05. Four hosts lie beyond the width calibration range, and only two have direct valid ASPCAP rotational velocities. The result supports a conditional spectral-width association without K2 labels or a velocity calibration. It does not identify inclination, magnetic broadening or material properties. Original analysis code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and separate-scratch regeneration steps are included. External record tables are excluded.

display.caption: Matched raw width contrasts and the separate absolute velocity calibration problem. Intervals resample complete pairs.
